source_name: ARES — Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů, open data + REST API
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance registry of all Czech economic subjects, exposing a public REST (and legacy XML) API plus full open-data dumps mandated by government decree. Essential for supplier verification in A2: resolve a supplier name in a tender award to a canonical IČO, legal form, address, registration date and source registers — the join key across VVZ, Registr smluv, TED and justice.cz.

source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (or.justice.cz) — Ministry of Justice
why_relevant: Authoritative commercial register plus the Collection of Deeds (sbírka listin) holding filed annual reports, financial statements, founding documents and statutory-body changes for every Czech legal entity. For A2 this converts a winning supplier into a verifiable financial and ownership profile — revenue scale, auditor, group structure — and reveals ownership changes that reshape incumbency.

source_name: dataor.justice.cz — OpenData ISVR (public registers bulk open data)
why_relevant: The bulk open-data distribution of the Czech public registers (ISVR), with exports in CSV/XML. Lets a scout build a local mirror of legal-entity master data — including historic states of directors, addresses and legal form — instead of scraping or.justice.cz page by page, which is the sustainable way to run supplier verification at scale.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — CDX Server API
why_relevant: Czech tender portals routinely purge or relocate expired notices (VVZ migrated to NIPEZ; old.vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz artefacts still circulate). The CDX Server API allows querying every archived capture of a URL or URL prefix with date, MIME and status-code filters, so a scout can recover the text of award notices, profile listings and supplier pages that no longer exist live — the only practical route to pre-migration Czech notice history.

source_name: zIndex — wiki metodiky hodnocení zadavatelů (wiki.zindex.cz)
why_relevant: Academic scoring methodology for Czech contracting authorities built on VVZ data, contracting-authority profiles and other tender sources over rolling three-year windows. Its wiki pages document exactly which data fields exist, where they are unreliable, and how supplier dependence (share of public contracts in total revenue) can be computed — a free methodological map of the CZ procurement data landscape and its quality traps.

source_name: Zakázky GOV (zakazky.gov.cz) — cross-system tender aggregation with alerts
why_relevant: State-side aggregation of tenders from multiple systems in one place, with free notification subscriptions for suppliers. Useful as a low-effort monitoring trigger and as a pointer to which underlying e-procurement system (NEN, E-ZAK, Tender arena, Gemin) a given authority uses — that mapping is what determines the right structured-collection route.

source_name: Gemin / vhodne-uverejneni.cz — third-party profil zadavatele platforms
why_relevant: A large share of Czech contracting authorities, including ČNB's referenced profile mirror on gemin.cz, host their statutory profil zadavatele on commercial platforms rather than NEN. These platforms carry the below-threshold contracts that never reach VVZ or TED and typically expose a profile XML export mandated by the profile decree — a necessary complement for full coverage of banking-sector buying.

source_name: GovTransparency — Czech/Hungarian/Slovak national procurement contract dataset
why_relevant: Academic research release of a cleaned CZ/HU/SK national contract-level dataset including a Corruption Risk Index and its components. Valuable as a ready-made historic panel for reconstructing long award series and testing incumbency persistence, without rebuilding the ETL from VVZ.

source_name: Portál otevřených dat Ministerstva financí (data.mf.gov.cz)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance's own open-data portal, publishing ARES bulk data and other fiscal datasets. Useful as a second, publisher-side index alongside NKOD for locating registry dumps and finance-sector datasets whose NKOD entries are incomplete or stale.

source_name: Erste Group Procurement (EGP) — group procurement subsidiary page, Erste Group Bank AG
source_subtype: corporate group procurement page / supplier document repository
why_relevant: EGP (Procurement Services Ges.m.b.H., Am Belvedere 1, Vienna) is the centralised sourcing function that manages the external spend of all majority-owned Erste Group entities, with its own subsidiaries in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia, Romania and Croatia. Vendor selection affecting Ceska sporitelna is therefore governed here, not on csas.cz. The page hosts the supplier document pack (Supplier General Documents, NDA, Supplier Audit Questionnaire, Supplier Performance Scorecard, Supplier Sustainability Scorecard, whistleblower channel) which encodes the qualification bar any CZ-facing vendor must clear.

source_name: Erste Group Services — group shared-service subsidiary page
why_relevant: Sibling shared-service entity to EGP; useful for mapping which back-office/service categories are pooled at group level (and therefore sourced centrally in Vienna) versus left to the Czech bank. Helps decide where to look for a given CZ vendor decision.

source_name: Erste Digital — group IT company (Vienna / Bratislava / Kosice / Prague)
why_relevant: Erste Digital (formed 1 July 2021 by merging Erste Group IT Solutions Austria and Erste Group IT International) develops and runs the IT solutions used across all Erste Group entities including Ceska sporitelna, and has a Prague location. IT/payments platform vendor decisions touching CZ are frequently made or executed here rather than at the Czech bank. Site carries a Czech-language section (/cs/services), giving local-language surface for the same actor.

source_name: Erste Group press releases (group-level deal and partnership announcements)
why_relevant: Group-level announcements are often the only public disclosure of CEE-wide vendor/partner arrangements that bind the Czech subsidiary — e.g. the Global Payments/CaixaBank/Erste merchant-acquiring joint venture covering Czech Republic, Slovakia and Romania with its headquarters in Prague, and the Erste Digital merger. Invisible to any csas.cz-only search.

source_name: KBC Group — Our suppliers (stakeholder interactions / procurement policy)
why_relevant: KBC is the parent of CSOB (Czech Republic is a KBC core market alongside Belgium, Slovakia, Hungary, Bulgaria). This is the group-level statement of how suppliers are engaged and by whom; KBC's Belgian procurement department (KDPB) handles commercial and legal negotiation and deliverables can only be ordered via formal KBC purchasing documents — i.e. a CZ-relevant contract may be signed in Brussels.

source_name: KBC Group Sustainability Code of Conduct for Suppliers (PDF)
why_relevant: Group-mandated qualification criteria that any CSOB-serving vendor must accept; CSOB explicitly applies sustainability as a qualitative evaluation criterion in its tender procedures, so this document is the upstream rulebook for CZ tender scoring.

source_name: KBC general terms & conditions and code of conduct for contracts (contracts_en document library)
why_relevant: Group contracting boilerplate (pricing, invoicing, purchasing documents issued by KDPB). Reveals the mechanics by which a group-level purchase order reaches a CZ-serving supplier and the standard commercial terms a competitor would face.

source_name: Société Générale Sourcing Hub (group e-sourcing portal)
why_relevant: SG owns ~60% of Komerční banka. All SG competitive processes are run online through this group e-sourcing tool, so RFPs whose delivery scope is Czech may be issued and adjudicated in Paris on this platform. Note self-registration has been withdrawn — suppliers must be created by SG teams — which is itself a market-access fact worth tracking.

source_name: Société Générale — Suppliers / Responsible sourcing pages
why_relevant: Group sourcing policy: neutrality, competitive online RFPs, responsible-purchasing commitments, and the end-to-end contact-to-payment process (including TradeShift for invoicing). Defines the rules under which a Komerční banka-scoped purchase is competed at group level.

source_name: RBI Group Supplier Code of Conduct (Raiffeisen Bank International)
why_relevant: Explicitly applies to all suppliers delivering goods, services or licences to or on behalf of any RBI business unit and subsidiary — which includes Raiffeisenbank a.s. in the Czech Republic. Mandatory contractual annex plus audit rights over suppliers and, in some cases, subcontractors: it is the group-level gate a CZ vendor must pass. Multiple dated versions (2023, 2024, 2025) allow change tracking.

source_name: RBI — Our network (group entity map)
why_relevant: Authoritative list of RBI's CEE subsidiaries and country presence (Vienna HQ, ~24 countries, 14 key markets). Needed to resolve which legal entity is contracting in a CEE-wide award and to confirm the Czech entity is in scope of a group category strategy.

source_name: Akirolabs customer story — RBI procurement transformation (plan-to-strategy digitalisation)
why_relevant: Vendor-published case study that discloses RBI procurement's operating model in unusual detail: a single source of truth for procurement across all 14 key markets, category strategies aligned across territories, digital stakeholder input. This is direct evidence that category decisions touching the Czech market are set centrally — exactly the mechanism this cell exists to track. Also identifies akirolabs as an incumbent procurement-tech vendor to the group.

source_name: CPOstrategy — RBI Procurement executive interview
why_relevant: Procurement trade press regularly interviews CEE bank CPOs, exposing strategy pillars (value-centric procurement, procurement systems/infrastructure, data, regulatory compliance and cybersecurity) and named toolchains. A reliable, low-cost channel for group-sourcing intelligence that never appears on CZ-language sites. Generalises: the same outlet family covers Erste, UniCredit and KBC procurement leaders.

source_name: UniCredit Services (group ICT/Operations/Real Estate/Security/Procurement shared services)
why_relevant: UniCredit Services is the group entity providing ICT, Operations, Real Estate, Security AND Procurement services across the group — the mechanism by which UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia vendor selection is centralised in Milan/Vienna. Important caveat to record: UniCredit Services S.C.p.A. was merged into UniCredit S.p.A. on 1 October 2022, so the microsite may be legacy and current sourcing sits inside UniCredit S.p.A. — treat the page as a historical/structural pointer and verify current placement.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia — press centre / tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: CZ-entity disclosure surface for group-driven technology and payments rollouts; the bilingual /cs/ and /en/ trees mean group announcements are often localised here first for the Czech and Slovak market. Cross-reference with UniCredit S.p.A. group releases to spot which CZ deployments were group framework decisions.

source_name: Registr smluv (smlouvy.gov.cz) — purchase orders and contracts naming foreign-parent bank entities
why_relevant: The Czech public contracts register surfaces contracts where a group-owned bank entity is a counterparty of a Czech public body, and the published PDFs leak internal procurement rules. A concrete example encountered: a redacted UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia order document setting out invoicing to Fakturace.ucetnictvi@unicreditgroup.cz, a zero-tolerance anti-corruption clause with a bar on suppliers suspected of corrupt conduct, and a requirement that Czech suppliers confirm they are not listed as unreliable VAT payers. That is group-authored procurement boilerplate reaching daylight through a CZ public register — a repeatable indirect route to group sourcing terms.

source_name: ARES / obchodní rejstřík — Czech registrations of group procurement and shared-service entities
why_relevant: Erste Group Procurement states it has its own subsidiary in the Czech Republic, and Erste Digital has a Prague site. Resolving those legal entities (name, IČO, registered office, statutory bodies, filed financial statements in the Sbírka listin) converts a vague 'group sourcing arm' into a named contracting party you can then trace through the contract register, court filings and job ads. Note: I did not confirm the specific Erste Group Procurement CZ entity name/IČO in this run.
